clue.text: Publisher is certainly half confused

indicators.note: only half of the word for certainty is muddled, so just its second pair of letters swaps order

blocks.note: taken as written
sure! is an affirmation meaning certainly

explanation.surface: A publisher admits to being somewhat muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: SURE stays half intact: SU keeps its place while RE becomes ER, giving IS + SU + ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An issuer is one who puts out or publishes something, such as stamps, shares or books.

clue.text: Grievance involving head of shop offering exchange, as before

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the grievance word holds the letter
head of points to the first letter of the following word

blocks.note: a score is a grudge or grievance, as in settling a score
the first letter of shop

explanation.surface: A complaint about the shop manager offering exchanges as he used to.
explanation.walkthrough: The shop's first letter goes just before the final letter of the grievance word. 'as before' marks the definition as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorse is an obsolete word for barter or exchange, found in Spenser.

clue.text: Predicted what gardener would need picked up?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a gardener needs a spade for digging

explanation.surface: A forecast of the tool a gardener would need to lift something.
explanation.walkthrough: Picked up looks like lifting a tool; it is the sound signal. Spae is a Scots word meaning to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: To spae is Scots for to prophesy, so spaed means foretold or predicted.

clue.text: Get rid of nuisance finally with old-fashioned V-sign?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: the final letter of nuisance
gest is an archaic word for gesture, and a V-sign is one example

explanation.surface: Someone sends off a nuisance with a rude two-fingered gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: A V-sign is a rude British hand gesture; the question mark flags it as one example of a gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: To egest is to discharge or expel waste from the body, a formal way of getting rid of something.

clue.text: Like a bird lying down but not quietly

indicators.note: but not means except, so the musical soft sign is left out

blocks.note: prostrate means lying flat
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Something resembles a bird resting on the ground, but not quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P from the front of PROSTRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostrate means having a beak (rostrum), so it describes being like a bird in that respect.

clue.text: Put foot down at home, confronting relation without hesitation

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the hesitation sound is taken away from the relative

blocks.note: in means at home
a sister is a relation
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone is firm at home when faced with a relative, without dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: Confronting here just means standing in front of, so the home word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To put your foot down is the idiom for taking a firm stand, which is what you do when you insist.

clue.text: Knight needing help hugging a female in the water?

indicators.note: hugging means holding inside, so the help word wraps around the a

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for knight
aid means help
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight comes to rescue a woman in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: A sits inside AID after its first two letters, then N goes in front: N + AI(A)D.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth, a female spirit living in rivers and springs.

clue.text: Top actor has reversal of role as a theatrical device

indicators.note: reversal of states plainly that the next word is read backwards

blocks.note: a star is a leading actor
a part is a role

explanation.surface: A leading actor swaps roles, as a theatrical gimmick.
explanation.definitionFit: A star trap is a stage trapdoor made of hinged segments, used to shoot an actor up onto the stage.

clue.text: Fifty lines laid out for trade event

indicators.note: laid out means arranged, so these letters are set out in a new order

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fifty lines of text are set out for a trade show.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-in is the selling of goods to retailers, typically at a promotional trade launch.

clue.text: More than one person on the box lets a secret out

definitions.text: More than one person on the box

indicators.note: out suggests something disordered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A television personality blurts out a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Lets a secret out reads as a phrase for leaking; out alone is the anagram signal. The box is slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Telecasters are broadcasters on television, people who appear on the box.

clue.text: Bawdy oaf for playing in an experimental theatre?

indicators.note: playing means fooling about, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rude lout performing on a fringe stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Playing looks like acting a part but signals the anagram. Broadway is New York's main theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-Broadway describes smaller, often experimental New York theatres away from the main commercial district.

clue.text: Peer at a dog spraying big erect plant

indicators.note: spraying scatters things about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone looks at a dog relieving itself against a large upright plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog spraying a tree is the picture; spraying is really the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The pagoda tree is a large Asian tree of the pea family, so a big upright plant.

clue.text: Horse and duck in Cornish river

indicators.note: in places the duck inside the river's name

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A horse and a duck seen on a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck sits inside the river: FA(O)L.
explanation.definitionFit: A foal is a young horse, so the general word serves as a definition by example.

clue.text: Observation of failure retrospectively limiting one

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so the word for failure is read from its end
limiting means bounding, so the failure word encloses the one

blocks.note: a lapse is a failure
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A report on a failure looked back on that restricts one person.
explanation.walkthrough: Observation looks like a remark; here it is the act of watching.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an old word for the act of spying or noticing, that is observation.

clue.text: Most indecent female has sudden fit of stubbornness

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
reest (Scots) is a sudden balking, a fit of stubbornness, as of a horse

explanation.surface: A very rude woman suddenly turns obstinate.
explanation.walkthrough: REEST is a Scots word found in Chambers, the Mephisto's dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Free can mean unrestrained in speech or conduct, close to risqué, so freest is the superlative of indecent.

clue.text: Maybe misrepresent the French, following fashion

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the French article is placed after the fashion word

blocks.note: garb is fashion or style of dress
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone gets the French wrong when talking about fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the definition as one example: to garble is one way to misrepresent.
explanation.definitionFit: To garble is to distort or mix up a message, which can misrepresent what was said.

clue.text: Watery edge that would have stone for butterfly

definitions.text: that would have stone for butterfly
definitions.note: describes a word which, with stone added, names a butterfly

blocks.note: first meaning: the edge of a body of water

blocks.clueFragment: that would have stone for butterfly
blocks.note: second meaning: the word that, given stone after it, names a yellow butterfly

explanation.walkthrough: The brimstone is a pale yellow butterfly; add STONE to the answer and you have it.
explanation.definitionFit: The brim is the edge or margin of a river or pool, and it is the first part of the butterfly brimstone.

clue.text: Industrial processors in plant had nasty pong to start with

indicators.note: to start with puts the bad-smell word at the front, ahead of the plant

blocks.note: smelt is a past tense of smell
ers is the bitter vetch, a plant

explanation.surface: Workers in a factory had a nasty smell to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant looks like a factory; it is ERS, the bitter vetch, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelters extract metal from ore by heating, so they are industrial processors.

clue.text: Plot needs arsenic dissolved — nothing more

indicators.note: something dissolved loses its form, so these letters reform in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
nothing is O, and more says it is added

explanation.surface: A murder plot requires arsenic dissolved in a drink, and nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline of a story or film, its plot.

clue.text: Lots of pieces of paper are put in order — handwritten stuff

indicators.note: putting in order rearranges things, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, something written by hand

explanation.surface: Many sheets of handwritten paper are being sorted.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a quantity of paper, about 500 sheets, and reams means a great deal of it.

clue.text: One of the old-style war missiles heartlessly lined up

indicators.note: heartlessly means without a heart, so the middle letter is taken out

blocks.clueFragment: One of the old-style war missiles
blocks.note: arrows were missiles of old warfare

explanation.surface: An antique weapon of war heartlessly arranged in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle R of ARROW goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Arow is an old word meaning in a row, so lined up.

clue.text: A sort of ridge for mites

blocks.note: taken as written
a carina is a keel-shaped ridge, as on a bird's breastbone

explanation.surface: A kind of ridge suitable for tiny creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Acarina is the zoological order containing mites and ticks.

clue.text: Sheath-like form with ring at front

indicators.note: at front says the ring is placed before the other part

blocks.note: O is ring-shaped
to form is to create

explanation.surface: A sheath-shaped object is made with a ring fitted at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocreate is a botanical term for having an ocrea, a sheath around a stem, so sheath-like.

clue.text: Theatrical turns restricted, cut short

indicators.note: cut short means docked at the end, so the last letter is removed

blocks.note: chained means restricted

explanation.surface: Stage performances limited and shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: Turns looks like acts in a variety show; it is ballet turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaîné is a ballet term for a series of quick turns along a line, a theatrical dance move.

clue.text: Presses down to make an impression, first to last

indicators.note: first to last tells you to move the opening letter to the end

blocks.note: to stamp is to make an impression

explanation.surface: Someone presses down hard to leave a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of STAMP moves to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamp is to pack something down firmly, as with tobacco in a pipe.

clue.text: OAPs regathered outside commercial hotel abroad

indicators.note: regathered means collected again in a fresh arrangement
outside means placed around, so the pensioners surround the commercial

blocks.note: OAPs are old-age pensioners
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Pensioners gather again outside a business hotel on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The commercial goes inside the shuffled pensioners, after their third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A posada is an inn or hotel in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Old-fashioned colour not entirely distinctive

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the next word is used

blocks.note: letters three to seven of distinctive

explanation.surface: A dated shade that is only partly distinctive.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinct is an archaic word for a tint or colour.

clue.text: Pronounce holy bishop "inferior"

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
less means inferior or lower in rank

explanation.surface: A bishop is declared holy, though he is quoted as inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless is to consecrate, declaring something holy.

clue.text: Tricked one with old coins

blocks.note: to be sold a pup is to be tricked
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone cheated a person using antique money.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldi is the plural of soldo, an old Italian coin.

clue.text: Pet bird given restraint

blocks.note: daw is a jackdaw
a tie is a restraint

explanation.surface: A pet bird is put on a tether.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet looks like it describes the bird, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawtie is a Scots word for a darling or favourite, someone treated as a pet.

clue.text: Sugar in lemonade's bad, putting off men somehow

indicators.note: putting off means sending away, so some letters are removed from the drink
somehow warns that the removed letters are not together but scattered through the word
bad suggests something gone wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sugar in the lemonade has gone off, discouraging the men somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M, E and N out of LEMONADES to leave LOADES, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An aldose is a monosaccharide containing an aldehyde group, such as glucose, so a kind of sugar.

clue.text: Term of office — time to practise once

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
enure is an old spelling of inure, to accustom by practice

explanation.surface: A term of office was once a period for practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks ENURE as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the period during which someone holds a post or office.

clue.text: Chemical spray on the wing

blocks.note: first meaning: a trade name for a growth regulator once sprayed on apples
second meaning: relating to wings

explanation.walkthrough: On the wing suggests flight, but here it simply means of the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Alar is both the brand name of a plant-growth chemical and an adjective meaning relating to wings.

clue.text: Sedan chair broken, no longer in good order?

indicators.note: something broken falls apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken sedan chair is no longer in working order.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by description: the broken chair has been made chaotic too.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchised means reduced to anarchy, lawless disorder, so no longer orderly.

clue.text: Turbulent couple of years involving China etc?

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the pair of letters wraps around the region

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, so two of them
China and its neighbours are in the East; the question mark flags definition by example

explanation.surface: A troubled two years in Chinese affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: EAST sits between the two Ys: Y(EAST)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeasty means frothing like fermenting yeast, hence restless or turbulent.

clue.text: Legendary Gaelic poet or knight

blocks.note: ossia is the Italian musical term for or, marking an alternative passage
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A legendary figure is described as either a Gaelic poet or a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link offering a choice, but it is the Italian musical term OSSIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossian is the legendary Irish and Scottish bard, son of Finn, made famous by Macpherson's poems.
